{{short description|On when a subvariety of a product of projective spaces is a product of varieties}}
In [[arithmetic geometry]], '''Faltings' product theorem''' gives sufficient conditions for a [[algebraic variety|subvariety]] of a product of [[projective space]]s to be a product of varieties in the projective spaces. It was introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Faltings|year=1991|authorlink=Gerd Faltings}} in his proof of Lang's conjecture that subvarieties of an [[abelian variety]] containing no translates of non-trivial abelian subvarieties have only finitely many rational points.

{{harvtxt|Evertse|1995}} and {{harvtxt|Ferretti|1996}} gave explicit versions of Faltings' product theorem.
